# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  gh-1934 (413-proof sessions): image blocks OUTSIDE the kept region —
  first seen before the LAST renumbering boundary — evict to
  `[image dropped: <key8>]` placeholders (payload-only, JSONL
  byte-identical); kept-region images ride on under the normal caps; the 413 recovery ladder
  (`agent_loop_image_recovery.dart` + `image_recovery.dart`, bounded at
  2 passes per response, each 413 halving the session's adaptive
  `images.maxBytesPerRequest`) drops the oldest images (pass 1), then
  strips ALL images including the current message (pass 2, latched
  session-wide), carrying the `[images] recovered from 413:` notice +
  model-visible note; classification lives in `image_overflow.dart`
  (`isPayloadTooLargeError`), surface wording in `image_drop_ux.dart`
  (`ImageDropReason.evicted`).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape (no eviction, no ladder). `agent_loop.dart` applies it in
  `_buildRequestContext` after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing
  repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  Conformance claims are the self-certification blind spot (gh-1834):
  when the final claim includes parity/conformance to a reference or
  specification (any domain), a "verified" item counts only with
  negative and combination checks — refused incompatible options,
  empty/corrupt inputs, boundary values, must-NOT-work cases — alongside
  happy paths; a blanket "everything matches" is not verified (prompt
  step 2.6, conditional: tasks with no conformance claim are
  unchanged).
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)

**ai-teammate** (2026-11-02):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the AC3 remediation vehicle re-flags an old release `--latest` — a fleet-wide `fa update` downgrade**

The remediation chain this PR wires up can move the `latest` badge **backwards**, which the PR itself declares must never happen:

1. `scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh:43` re-requests the tag's **"Sign release checksums"** job:
   ```bash
   gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --job "$job_id"
   ```
2. That job's "Upload provenance assets" step ends with an **unconditional** flip (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:4515`):
   ```bash
   gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
   ```
   A job rerun re-executes **all** its steps with the original run's ref, so `GITHUB_REF_NAME` is the (possibly old) tag.
3. `gh release edit --latest` is "**Explicitly mark the release as 'Latest'**" (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_edit) — it designates that release as Latest *regardless of whether a newer release exists*.
4. The new workflow explicitly advertises the dangerous path as its primary use (`.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml:16`): *"dispatching it for v1.0.680 IS the AC3 remediation"*. Once any newer release exists, dispatching drift-watch for an older drifted tag re-flags that older release as Latest → every `fa update` client "updates" **down** to it (the re-signed manifest makes the downgrade pass provenance verification).

The PR's own invariant text: *"A PUBLISHED release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade"* (`scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh:57-58`, same wording in `test/release_publish_imutability_test.dart:10`). The attach path enforces it; the remediation path reintroduces it.

Note the scheduled/`release: published` paths are safe (they only ever target the current latest), so this bites exactly the documented manual-remediation flow.

**Suggested fix** — make the flip conditional in the provenance job (keeps the gh-1801 publish point and the AC4 pin intact):

```bash
is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
is_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$is_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
  gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
else
  # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is already
  # correct — never drag the latest badge backwards (gh-2042).
  gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
fi
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-11-02):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: untrusted `${{ }}` interpolation into `run:` shell — use env indirection**

The "Resolve target release" step interpolates `${{ inputs.tag }}` and `${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}` directly into a `run:` block:

```yaml
if [ -n "${{ inputs.tag }}" ]; then
  tag="${{ inputs.tag }}"
```

and the resolved value is then re-interpolated in the two downstream `run:` steps as `"${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}"`. This is the classic GitHub Actions script-injection pattern: a tag value containing shell metacharacters (`` ` ``, `$( )`, `;`) executes in the runner — a job holding `contents: read` + `actions: write` + `issues: write`.

Both `workflow_dispatch` and release publishing currently require repo write access, so this is not an external-attacker path — but it is exactly the hazard class this repo's SEC-08 posture (explicit least-privilege blocks in this very workflow) works to avoid, and GitHub's security-hardening guide calls for env-var indirection for *all* untrusted template values.

**Fix**:

```yaml
- name: Resolve target release
  id: target
  env:
    DISPATCH_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
    RELEASE_EVENT_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail
    if [ -n "$DISPATCH_TAG" ]; then
      tag="$DISPATCH_TAG"
    elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "release" ]; then
      tag="$RELEASE_EVENT_TAG"
    ...
```

and pass the result into the check/remediate steps the same way (`env: TAG: ${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}` → `"$TAG"`). Repo precedent exists both ways (`release-appstore.yml` interpolates inputs directly — equally flaggable), so this is hardening-for-consistency, not a regression unique to this PR.

```bash

so the atomicity the gate documents and the tests pin is never exercised in production:

- With assets `[a.zip, fa-bad.tar.gz]` on a PUBLISHED release, the first gate call clobbers `a.zip` before the second call refuses `fa-bad.tar.gz` — a partial mutation the single-call contract forbids (benign for the manifest only because the partial case is non-fa, i.e. by accident of ordering, not by construction).

**Fix** — one call for the whole list (the gate already loops internally and refuses before any upload):

```

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Release asset immutability gate (gh-2042, AC1): the single attach path for
+# `fa-*` assets onto a GitHub Release.
+#
+# The v1.0.680 incident: the daily build-macos train resolved a tag whose
+# release was ALREADY PUBLISHED (the same-tag convergence race — the tag
+# train published while the daily train's slow self-hosted legs were still
+# building) and re-attached fresh fa-macos-arm64 assets ~2-3h AFTER the
+# signed SHA256SUMS was attached. The manifest never re-ran, so every
+# `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on the train failed for every
+# macOS-arm64 user. A published release must be IMMUTABLE for `fa-*`
+# assets: the signed manifest vouches for exactly the bytes that were on
+# the release when release-provenance signed it.
+#
+# Verdicts (per call, all-or-nothing — a partial attach would still drift
+# the manifest):
+#   release missing        → allow (the caller lazy-drafts first; a raw
+#                            upload to a missing release errors loudly)
+#   release is a DRAFT     → attach everything --clobber (the gh-1801 flow,
+#                            unchanged: publish stays provenance-owned)
+#   release is PUBLISHED   → for every listed asset:
+#                              - name already attached → immutable SKIP
+#                                (the release-twin binaries re-run: same
+#                                tag commit, asset already shipped)
+#                              - name not attached, matches `fa-*` →
+#                                REFUSE the whole call with a loud
+#                                ::error:: (post-publish attach must
+#                                target a DRAFT / next-version or re-run
+#                                release-provenance for the tag)
+#                              - name not attached, NOT fa-* → attach
+#                                (store AAB/IPA/APK + DMG refreshers are
+#                                deliberately not provenance-covered,
+#                                see scripts/release_required_assets.txt)
+#   anything undeterminable (API blip, unparseable verdict) → fail CLOSED
+#
+# SHA256SUMS(.sig) are NOT fa-* assets: release-provenance's raw
+# `gh release upload` of the manifest is the sanctioned post-publish
+# remediation (re-hash the current bytes, re-sign) and stays outside this
+# gate by design (gh-2042 AC3).
+#
+# Usage: release_asset_gate.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
+# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+tag="${1:?usage: release_asset_gate.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
+repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
+shift
+assets=("$@")
+if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "::error::release_asset_gate.sh called with zero assets for $tag — a caller bug: resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+err=$(mktemp)
+trap 'rm -f "$err"' EXIT
+state_json=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft,assets 2>"$err") || {
+  if grep -qi "not found" "$err"; then

+    # (release_lazy_draft.sh / the create in release_attach_or_create.sh).
+    # Attempt the upload — a still-missing release errors loudly in gh.
+    for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
+      gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
+    done
+    echo "✅ gate: release $tag absent — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) (draft-first flow)"
+    exit 0
+  fi
+  echo "::error::cannot determine the release state of $tag ($(cat "$err")) — refusing to attach (gh-2042 fail-closed: an undeterminable verdict must never mutate a release)" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+if printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -e '.isDraft == false' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  # PUBLISHED — the immutability contract.
+  attached=$(printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -r '.assets[].name')
+  refused=()
+  skipped=()
+  uploadable=()
+  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
+    name=$(basename "$asset")
+    if printf '%s\n' "$attached" | grep -qxF "$name"; then
+      skipped+=("$name")
+    elif [[ "$name" == fa-* ]]; then
+      refused+=("$name")
+    else
+      uploadable+=("$asset")
+    fi

+  fi
+  for name in "${skipped[@]:-}"; do
+    [ -n "$name" ] || continue
+    echo "✅ gate: $name already on the published release $tag — immutable skip (gh-2042)"
+  done
+  for asset in "${uploadable[@]:-}"; do
+    [ -n "$asset" ] || continue

+  done
+  exit 0

+  done

+  exit 0
+fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release drift check (gh-2042, AC2): re-download every `fa-*` asset of a
# release and diff sha256 against the signed SHA256SUMS.
#
# The v1.0.680 incident: assets were re-attached to the published release
# ~2-3h AFTER the manifest was signed, so the manifest no longer described
# the shipped bytes and every `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on
# the train failed. This is the CI-side twin of bin/self_manage.dart's
# verifyReleaseProvenance — same manifest, same digest comparison — run
# after every release publish and on a schedule
# (.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml). Drift = red run + a details
# file the remediation step pages from + an auto re-request of
# release-provenance. Drift must page, not linger.
#
# Checks (any hit = drift, exit 1):
#   - SHA256SUMS / SHA256SUMS.sig present on the release (no signature = no
#     provenance at all — the SEC-07 #795 fail-closed class);
#   - every manifest entry's digest matches the downloaded bytes
#     (sha256sum -c);
#   - the manifest covers EXACTLY the release's fa-* set (an fa-* asset on
#     the release that the manifest does not list is a stale manifest — the
#     v1.0.680 `-mac.zip` shape; a manifest entry the release no longer
#     serves is a missing asset — the gh-1832 shape).
#
# Exit codes (gh-2042 review: infra is NOT drift evidence):
#   0  clean — every fa-* asset matches the signed SHA256SUMS;
#   1  DRIFT — a verdict a human must see (the workflow pages from the
#      details file + auto re-requests release-provenance);
#   2  INFRA — the assets could not be downloaded (transport error after a
#      retry): red run, but NO drift page (the next scheduled run
#      re-checks; the remediation step only pages on a non-empty details
#      file, which an infra failure never writes).
#
# Usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN,
#      FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR (tests only: verify a pre-populated directory
#      instead of downloading), FA_DRIFT_DETAILS (drift details file, the
#      remediation step pages from it; default drift-details.txt in the CWD),
#      FA_DRIFT_RETRY_SLEEP (seconds between download retries; default 2).
#
# GNU-bound (sha256sum -c, find -printf, comm): this check targets the
# ubuntu-latest workflow runner — it fails confusingly if run locally on
# macOS/BSD.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
details="${FA_DRIFT_DETAILS:-drift-details.txt}"

drift=()
report() { # report <line>: collects the drift finding + names it in the details file
  drift+=("$1")
  printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$details"
}

# The details reset runs BEFORE any download (gh-2042 review): a check that
# dies mid-download must never leave stale checkout content behind for the
# remediation step to page as if it were today's drift.
rm -f "$details"

workdir="${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-$(mktemp -d)}"

# Download with a transient-blip guard (gh-2042 review): retry once on
# transport failures (502, rate limit, ...) and treat ONLY an explicit
# not-found / no-match verdict as a deterministic "absent" (rc 2). Any
# other failure after the retry is infra (rc 1).
gh_dl() { # gh_dl <pattern> → 0 downloaded, 2 deterministic absent, 1 infra
  local pattern="$1" attempt err rc
  for attempt in 1 2; do
    err=$(mktemp)
    rc=0
    gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --dir "$workdir" --pattern "$pattern" 2>"$err" || rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
      rm -f "$err"
      return 0
    fi
    if grep -Eqi 'not found|no assets match' "$err"; then
      rm -f "$err"
      return 2
    fi
    rm -f "$err"
    if [ "$attempt" -lt 2 ]; then
      sleep "${FA_DRIFT_RETRY_SLEEP:-2}"
    fi
  done
  return 1
}

if [ -z "${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-}" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$workdir"
  # The manifest and its signature ride their own pattern: `fa-*` does not
  # match them, and BOTH must be on the release for provenance to exist.
  fa_rc=0
  sha_rc=0
  gh_dl 'fa-*' || fa_rc=$?
  gh_dl 'SHA256SUMS*' || sha_rc=$?
  if [ "$fa_rc" -eq 1 ] || [ "$sha_rc" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "::error::release drift check could not download the assets of $tag (transport error after retry) — an infra blip is NOT drift evidence: failing WITHOUT a drift page; the next scheduled run re-checks" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
fi

if [ ! -f "$workdir/SHA256SUMS" ]; then
  report "SHA256SUMS is NOT on release $tag — provenance can never be verified (SEC-07 #795 fail-closed class)"
else
  if [ ! -f "$workdir/SHA256SUMS.sig" ]; then
    report "SHA256SUMS.sig is NOT on release $tag — an unsigned manifest is not provenance"
  fi
  if ! (cd "$workdir" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS > "$workdir/sha-check.log" 2>&1); then
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      case "$line" in
        *FAILED*|*failed*)
          report "digest drift: $line"
          ;;
      esac
    done < "$workdir/sha-check.log"
  fi
fi

# Set diff, both directions: the manifest must cover EXACTLY the fa-* set
# actually on the release. The names are read LINE-WISE (gh-2042 review):
# release asset names may contain spaces, and a word-split loop would
# report one bogus per-word "asset" instead of the whole name.
manifest_names=$(sed -n 's/^[0-9a-fA-F]\{64\}[[:space:]]\+\*\?//p' "$workdir/SHA256SUMS" 2>/dev/null || true)
local_names=$(find "$workdir" -maxdepth 1 -name 'fa-*' -type f -printf '%f\n' 2>/dev/null | sort)
unlisted=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$manifest_names" | sort -u) | sed '/^$/d')
uncovered=$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$manifest_names" | sort -u) | sed '/^$/d')
while IFS= read -r name; do
  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
  report "stale manifest: fa asset $name is on the release but NOT in SHA256SUMS (attached after signing?)"
done <<< "$unlisted"
while IFS= read -r name; do
  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
  report "missing asset: SHA256SUMS lists $name but the release no longer serves it (gh-1832 shape)"
done <<< "$uncovered"

if [ "${#drift[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "drift-details file: $details" >&2
  for line in "${drift[@]}"; do
    echo "::error::release drift on $tag: $line (gh-2042 AC2 — the signed SHA256SUMS no longer matches the shipped assets; remediation: re-run release-provenance for the tag)" >&2
  done
  exit 1
fi

echo "✅ release drift check passed for $tag: every fa-* asset matches the signed SHA256SUMS ($(printf '%s\n' "$local_names" | grep -c . || true) assets)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release drift remediation (gh-2042, AC2): when the drift check finds a
# published release whose assets no longer match the signed SHA256SUMS, this
# step (a) auto re-requests the release-provenance job for the tag — the job
# re-hashes the CURRENT assets and re-signs the manifest, which is also the
# AC3 v1.0.680 remediation mechanism — and (b) pages a DEDUPLICATED issue so
# drift never lingers silently.
#
# The re-request targets the SIGN JOB (`gh run rerun --job`), never the
# whole tag run: a full rerun would rebuild + re-attach every asset, which
# the immutability gate (scripts/release_asset_gate.sh, gh-2042 AC1) now
# refuses on a published release — and a rebuild is not what remediation
# needs anyway (the shipped bytes are the truth; only the manifest is stale).
#
# Paging FIRST-CLASS: the issue is filed even when the re-request fails or
# the tag run cannot be found (deleted history, PR-only branch names) — the
# only total failure of this step is the issue filing itself failing.
#
# Issue dedup: exact title `[release-drift] SHA256SUMS drift on <tag>` —
# an open match gets a comment (a fresh data point), never a duplicate.
#
# Usage: release_drift_remediate.sh <tag> <drift-details-file>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_drift_remediate.sh <tag> <drift-details-file>}"
details_file="${2:?usage: release_drift_remediate.sh <tag> <drift-details-file>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

details="(drift details unavailable)"
[ -f "$details_file" ] && details=$(cat "$details_file")

rerun_status="(re-request not possible: no completed workflow run found for tag $tag on ci.yml)"
# `// 0` (not `// ""`): jq encodes the empty STRING as `""` — with quotes —
# which would defeat the emptiness guard. 0 is never a real run id.
run_id=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml --branch "$tag" \
  --limit 30 --json databaseId,conclusion \
  --jq '[.[] | select(.conclusion != null)] | first | .databaseId // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "$run_id" != "0" ] && [ -n "$run_id" ]; then
  job_id=$(gh api "repos/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id/jobs" --paginate \
    --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name == "Sign release checksums") | .id' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "${job_id:-}" ]; then
    if gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --job "$job_id" 2>/dev/null; then
      rerun_status="release-provenance re-requested: run $run_id, job $job_id (it re-hashes the current assets and re-signs — gh-2042 AC2/AC3)"
    else
      rerun_status="re-request FAILED: gh run rerun $run_id --job $job_id was rejected — rerun the 'Sign release checksums' job manually"
    fi
  else
    rerun_status="re-request FAILED: no 'Sign release checksums' job on run $run_id — rerun release-provenance for the tag manually"
  fi
fi

title="[release-drift] SHA256SUMS drift on $tag"
body="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-drift-body.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$body"' EXIT
{
  echo "## $title"
  echo
  echo "$details"
  echo
  echo "**Auto-remediation (gh-2042 AC2):** $rerun_status"
  echo
  echo "If the drift persists after the re-run, an attach path replaced fa-* assets on the published release again — find it and gate it (scripts/release_asset_gate.sh). Until the manifest matches the shipped bytes, \`fa update\` / install.sh provenance verification fails for this train."
} > "$body"

# Dedup: exact open-title match (the inject-failure verify pattern) →
# comment; otherwise create. Best-effort label so the issues are filterable.
existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --limit 200 \
  --json number,title --jq '.[] | select(.title == $t) | .number' --arg t "$title" 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
  gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null \
    || { echo "::error::drift on $tag: could not comment the open drift issue #$existing — page the release owner manually" >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "✅ drift issue updated: #$existing (dedup — no duplicate filed)"
else
  gh label create release-drift --repo "$repo" --color D97706 --description "Published release assets drifted from the signed SHA256SUMS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --label release-drift \
    --body-file "$body" >/dev/null \
    || { echo "::error::drift on $tag: could not file the drift issue — page the release owner manually" >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "✅ drift issue filed for $tag — paged (gh-2042 AC2: drift must not linger)"
fi
===
# gh-2042 — release drift watch (AC2 + the AC3 remediation vehicle).
#
# The v1.0.680 incident: assets were re-attached to the ALREADY-PUBLISHED
# release ~2-3h after the signed SHA256SUMS was attached; the manifest never
# re-ran and every `fa update` provenance check on the train failed for
# macOS-arm64. The attach paths are now gated
# (scripts/release_asset_gate.sh, gh-2042 AC1) — this workflow is the
# detection backstop for ANY drift that still reaches a published release:
#
#   - after every release publish (the `release: published` event fires when
#     release-provenance flips the draft — the manifest is on board by then):
#     verify the tag's shipped bytes against its signed SHA256SUMS;
#   - on a DAILY schedule: the same check for the latest published release
#     (the one `fa update` serves) — drift must page, not linger;
#   - on demand (workflow_dispatch with a tag): the manual remediation
#     vehicle — dispatching it for v1.0.680 IS the AC3 remediation: the
#     check detects the stale manifest and the remediation step auto
#     re-requests the release-provenance job, which re-hashes the CURRENT
#     assets and re-signs. The provenance flip is guarded (gh-2042
#     review): re-signing an OLD tag publishes the corrected manifest
#     without ever dragging the `latest` badge backwards onto it.
#
# On drift the run goes red, a deduplicated issue pages the owner, and the
# "Sign release checksums" job of the tag's ci.yml run is re-requested
# (scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh — job-scoped rerun, never a full run:
# a full rerun would rebuild + re-attach, which the AC1 gate refuses on a
# published release). Only DRIFT pages: a transport/infra blip fails the
# check red WITHOUT a details file and the remediation step stays silent —
# an infra error is not drift evidence (gh-2042 review).
name: Release drift watch

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Daily, offset from the other crons (ci 23 */2, daily-publish 17 5,
    # nightly 17 3 / 17 7).
    - cron: '51 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Tag to verify (empty = the latest published release). Dispatch for a stale-manifest tag IS the provenance re-sign remediation (gh-2042 AC3).'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# SEC-08: explicit minimal default — the job declares its own block below.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release-drift-watch
  cancel-in-progress: false # a drift check is never preempted mid-page

jobs:
  drift-watch:
    name: Verify assets match the signed SHA256SUMS
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read # download the release assets
      actions: write # re-request the release-provenance job on drift
      issues: write # the deduplicated drift page
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Resolve target release
        id: target
        env:
          # gh-2042 review: untrusted template values ride env-var
          # indirection, never direct ${{ }} interpolation into the run:
          # shell (the GitHub Actions security-hardening guide's script
          # injection pattern — this job holds actions:write + issues:write).
          DISPATCH_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_EVENT_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$DISPATCH_TAG" ]; then
            tag="$DISPATCH_TAG"
            echo "source=dispatch"
          elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "release" ]; then
            tag="$RELEASE_EVENT_TAG"
            echo "source=release event"
          else
            tag=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name)
            echo "source=schedule (latest published)"
          fi
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "verifying $tag"

      - name: Verify assets against the signed manifest (gh-2042 AC2)
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}
          FA_DRIFT_DETAILS: drift-details.txt
        run: bash scripts/release_drift_check.sh "$TAG"

      - name: Page + auto re-request release-provenance (drift never lingers)
        if: failure()
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-2042 review: only DRIFT pages. A transport/infra failure
          # exits the check red WITHOUT writing the details file — the run
          # stays red but files no issue and re-requests nothing (the next
          # scheduled run re-checks; the release's provenance is intact).
          if [ -s drift-details.txt ]; then
            bash scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh "$TAG" drift-details.txt
          else
            echo "red WITHOUT drift details — transport/infra failure, not drift: no page, no re-request (the next scheduled run re-checks)"
          fi

name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —

- name: Upload extension to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-extension.zip"
          cp build/fa-extension.zip "$asset"
          ls -lh "$asset"

          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first, NEVER publish here. The
          # extension zip is not a `fa update` asset — and even a CLI
          # asset alone would not make the release servable: the SIGNED
          # SHA256SUMS only lands in the tag-run's release-provenance job,
          # which owns the --draft=false --latest flip. Create the draft
          # with the curated notes + the draft-owner marker (so the guard
          # step below can reclaim it on failure) and upload.
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"
          # gh-2042 AC1: the immutability gate owns the attach — a
          # PUBLISHED release (the same-tag convergence race) skips
          # attached assets and refuses unattached fa-* assets loud
          # instead of silently drifting the signed SHA256SUMS.
          bash scripts/release_asset_gate.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "$asset"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): this job creates releases,
      # so a failed/cancelled run must not leave one behind as a draft.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the guard closes the flip for post-guard commits only — a re-requested OLD job still runs the unconditional `--latest` flip**

This conditional flip correctly protects every rerun of a job whose run's commit contains it (`gh run rerun` re-executes the job with the workflow file as it existed at the original run's commit SHA — GitHub re-run semantics, https://docs.github.com/en/actions/managing-workflow-runs/re-running-workflows-and-jobs: a re-run uses the same `GITHUB_SHA`/`GITHUB_REF` of the original event).

But `scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh` re-requests the **tag's own historical run** (`gh run list --branch "$tag"` → `gh run rerun --job`), and the drift-watch workflow header explicitly advertises dispatching for **v1.0.680** — a tag minted *before* this PR — as THE AC3 remediation vehicle. v1.0.680's "Sign release checksums" job re-runs the OLD ci.yml, whose flip is still the unconditional `gh release edit --draft=false --latest`.

Concretely:

- **Today**: safe — v1.0.680 is still the Latest release, so even the old unconditional flip only reasserts the current badge, and AC3 (re-sign the shipped bytes) works as intended.
- **After the next release ships**: a newer tag is Latest. If any pre-guard tag drifts and someone dispatches drift-watch for it (exactly the documented flow), the re-requested old job re-flags that **older** release as Latest → every `fa update` client "updates" **down** onto it, with a freshly valid signature that passes provenance. That is the same fleet-wide downgrade the r1 BLOCKING thread (now resolved) was about — the guard fixes it for new tags but the remediation vehicle's primary historical use case re-enters through the old workflow file.

Suggested fixes (either one closes the window):

1. Give remediation its own tiny workflow on `main` (`release-re-sign.yml`): download the release's `fa-*` + assert required assets → sign → upload → guarded flip — it always runs the guard, regardless of the tag's age; `release_drift_remediate.sh` dispatches it instead of `gh run rerun --job`.
2. Or, in `release_drift_remediate.sh`, refuse the re-request when the tag's run predates the guard (e.g. probe the run's head SHA for `--latest` gating in its ci.yml) and degrade to a human-paged instruction in the drift issue.

Until one of these lands, the drift-watch header's claim — "re-signing an OLD tag publishes the corrected manifest without ever dragging the `latest` badge backwards onto it" — holds only while the old tag is still Latest.

💡 **SUGGESTION: a `sha256sum -c` failure with zero `FAILED` lines currently reports no drift**

The contract at the top of the script is "any hit = drift, exit 1", but this matcher only promotes lines containing `FAILED`/`failed`. If `sha256sum -c` exits non-zero for a reason that prints no such line — e.g. a manifest with CRLF line endings ("no properly formatted checksum lines found"), or other corruption that names nothing — `drift[]` stays empty. In those shapes the sed set-diff usually still catches the mismatch (I probed CRLF and malformed-hash manifests: the names don't extract/match, so the stale-manifest loop fires and the run stays red), so this is defense-in-depth, not an observed hole — but a corrupted manifest that *does* still sed-match the local set would pass with the ✅ success line.

Cheap catch-all:

```bash
  if ! (cd "$workdir" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS > "$workdir/sha-check.log" 2>&1); then
    reported=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      case "$line" in
        *FAILED*|*failed*)
          report "digest drift: $line"
          reported=1
          ;;
      esac
    done < "$workdir/sha-check.log"
    # gh-2042 hardening: a failed verification that named nothing is still drift —
    # never let a nonzero sha-check pass silently.
    [ "$reported" -eq 1 ] || report "SHA256SUMS failed verification without a named FAILED line — manifest shape is suspect (see $workdir/sha-check.log)"
  fi
```

## Review summary — PR #2045 (gh-2042, re-review round 2)

**Verdict: `REQUEST_CHANGES`** — 1 🚨 BLOCKING, 1 ⚠️ IMPORTANT, 2 💡 SUGGESTIONS.

All 7 r1 threads were mechanically verified fixed in this diff (guarded provenance flip at ci.yml:4527-4536, residue deleted + gitignored, hermetic `_runCheck`, env-indirected workflow, one gate call for the whole asset list, infra≠drift retry design, line-wise set-diff). The PR's own verify command passes **63/63** locally, `bash -n` is clean on all four scripts, and no residue regenerates after a test run.

The blocking finding is the **red CI gate on the reviewed head `29ddbe76`**: `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` (gh-1903 orphan-cancel) hit a 30s `TimeoutException` → "process did not exit after signal" in Core tests shard 3/4. The file is untouched by this PR and looks like a load flake in a real-subprocess SIGINT test — but the gate is red on this exact head and the PR description's "4 pre-existing reds" list (all `test/integration/` PTY/yolo tests) does not cover it.

The important finding is a **residual `--latest` downgrade window**: `release_drift_remediate.sh` re-requests the tag's *own* "Sign release checksums" job, and GitHub re-runs a job with the workflow file from the original run's commit — so every tag minted before this PR re-runs the *old* unconditional `--latest` flip. Safe today (v1.0.680 is still Latest), but after the next release ships, the documented manual-remediation flow for an older drifted tag drags the badge backwards. Fix suggestion in the thread: a dedicated re-sign workflow on `main`, or gating the re-request on the run's commit containing the guard.

CodeGraph was unavailable in this environment; impact analysis used git/grep fallback (documented per guidelines).

**Artifacts**: `outputs/pr_review.json` · `outputs/pr_review_general.md` · `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment_1_residual_latest_downgrade.md` · `comment_2_sha_check_no_failed_line.md` · `comment_3_test_filename_typo.md`

**Negative/conformance checks run**: failing-test attribution (untouched file), residue-absence + gitignore pins, malformed/CRLF-manifest probes against the drift check (set-diff backstop holds → finding downgraded to suggestion), rerun-semantics reasoning cited with the GitHub docs URL for the IMPORTANT finding.
